text:
jon: Running nsys capture for the KV-cache hot path and the perf timeline shows a bunch of kernels with no file/line info. stack frames are there but source:0 or just empty. anyone seen this recently?

maya: ugh. do you have the exact nsys command and the container image? most of the time it's either CUPTI mismatch or stripped debug info inside the image.

jon: repro steps:
```
# build/runtime image: REDWOOD_RUNTIME:latest (distroless-ish)
docker run --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash redwood/runtime:latest
# on host
nsys profile --output ks_kvcache --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt ./bin/runtime --serve-config cfg.yaml
```
nsys summary shows kernels like conv1_fwd.torch with addr but no file/line.

sam: try `nsys profile --capture-range cublas,nvtx --sample=none`? also share `cuptiGetVersion` output from the container. CUPTI-host mismatch kills line mapping often.

jon: grabbed CUPTI: inside container /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so -> version reported 11.8.0 but host driver stack is 470.x (old). Could that cause it?

maya: yes. CUPTI client in container needs to match the host driver for reliable activity APIs. But for symbolization you also need unstripped object files or debuginfo installed and accessible at the same path recorded at build. distortion can happen with containerized pathmaps.

olivia: we started compressing debug info into .debug files and then ran `strip --strip-debug` in the image to save bytes. that might remove lineinfo. cc @jon maybe your dockerfile has a `--strip-all` step.

jon: I DO have `strip --strip-unneeded` in the final stage. but the build produced separate .debug files (we used objcopy --only-keep-debug). the problem is in the distroless final image we didn't copy /usr/lib/debug or the .debug files.

maya: two quick checks: (1) run nsys on the host binary (not container) to see if symbolization works, (2) bind-mount /usr/lib/debug into the container and re-run nsys to confirm it's a missing debug file issue.

jon: did the host run: host nsight shows file/lines fine. bind-mount test: `docker run --rm -v /usr/lib/debug:/usr/lib/debug:ro ...` re-run nsys -> lines return for several kernels! so it's definitely missing debuginfo in container at the same path.

sam: nice triage. follow-ups: ensure build preserves either inline debug or provide a debuglink that points to installed .debug files inside the image. Also check `--build-id` handling; some distrs relocate .build-id lookups to /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/xx/yy`. If that path isn't present, addr2line can't resolve.

jon: question: is there a way for nsys/CUPTI to give better diagnostics for missing symbols? it just shows unnamed frames.

maya: nsys has `--debugger-mode` and there's an env `NSIGHT_DEBUG_SERVICE`? but it's not super verbose. For symbolization debugging, run `addr2line -e <binary> 0xADDR` for a hot address; if addr2line can't find it, it's definitely a debug-info problem. Example: `addr2line -Cfipe /opt/redwood/bin/runtime 0x7f1a2b3c` -> prints "??:0" when missing.

olivia: also consider the CUPTI side: if CUPTI callbacks are returning limited info because of a driver mismatch you'll see missing mapping for some CUDA kernels (jit/PTX paths). but since host profiling worked, this is 95% container debuginfo.

jon: fixed locally by adding a `COPY --from=debug-build /usr/src/app/.debug /usr/lib/debug` step. re-ran nsys and perfetto timelines look clean. submitting a small PR to update the runtime image.

ci-bot: CI job started: https://ci.internal.redwood/reports/1847621111-kvcache-symbols-fix -> tests: profile-unit, image-smoke

sam: once PR lands, can we add a small test that runs addr2line on a known kernel address during image build to assert debuginfo present? tiny smoke test would avoid regressions.

maya: good idea. also add docs in eng-runtime on the expected debuginfo layout and CUPTI/driver alignment checklist for people doing traces.

jon: thanks all. saved me hours. will link PR and the quick repro script in the PR description. :thumbsup:
